answer: A mechanism that actually bites: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because cipher only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, crystal is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
